comments.author: Anil Rathi
comments.message: feels salesy. The problem: little to no value in "applying" for a job, what about "applying skills"? to prove you are a fit and worthy of that job - reveal human capability and purpose. Organizations signal to job seekers that didn't get a callback they are more than a resume.

proposals.before:
Most professional development programs leave you with a certificate.
@[Innovation Challenge®](urn:li:organization:11786165) programs leave you with a network, a story, and sometimes, a career.

I still hear the stories about our alumni all the time:

🔹A finalist who’s now leading innovation at a major bank.
🔹Participants who stayed in touch with execs from Hilton and Whirlpool, even years later.
🔹Entrepreneurs who trace the launch of their ventures back to a single challenge experience.

One of our participants, during the final round, said to me:

“One question, 10 different perspectives on the same problem. It cracked open how I think!”

That’s the power of these challenges.

Sure, they surface great ideas, but more importantly, they activate people.

• They build networks.
• They unlock confidence.
• They reframe what’s possible.

An innovation challenge can be a turning point.

For companies, it's a chance to spot potential and build relationships early.
For participants, it’s often where the next chapter begins.

Who’s someone you met early in your career who changed your professional trajectory?
proposals.after:
Applying for a job usually means dropping a resume into a void and hoping someone calls back.
@[Innovation Challenge®](urn:li:organization:11786165) programs work the other way around: instead of applying for a job, people get to apply their skills — proving they’re a fit by revealing the human capability and purpose a resume can’t show.

I still hear the stories about our alumni all the time:

🔹A finalist who’s now leading innovation at a major bank.
🔹Participants who stayed in touch with execs from Hilton and Whirlpool, even years later.
🔹Entrepreneurs who trace the launch of their ventures back to a single challenge experience.

One of our participants, during the final round, said to me:

“One question, 10 different perspectives on the same problem. It cracked open how I think!”

That’s the power of these challenges.

Sure, they surface great ideas, but more importantly, they let people show who they really are.

• They reveal capability a resume misses.
• They unlock confidence.
• They reframe what’s possible.

And they change how organizations show up, too.

The best ones send a signal to everyone who takes part — even those who don’t get a callback — that they are so much more than a resume.

For companies, it's a chance to see potential early and treat people like people.
For participants, it’s a place to be valued for what they can actually do.

When did someone look past your resume and see what you were truly capable of?
proposals.rationale: Anil felt the original read as salesy and wanted the frame shifted from the value of 'applying for a job' toward 'applying skills' — proving fit/worthiness by revealing human capability and purpose — plus the idea that organizations should signal to candidates who don't get a callback that they are more than a resume. Ambiguous/subjective ask, so this is a best-effort rewrite: (1) dropped the 'leave you with... a career' promise that read as the most salesy line and reopened on the applicant's real problem (a resume dropped into a void); (2) reframed the core value prop around applying skills to prove fit and reveal human capability + purpose; (3) reworked the bullet list from outcomes ('build networks') toward revealing capability a resume misses; (4) added a stanza on organizations signaling to everyone who takes part — even non-callback candidates — that they are more than a resume; (5) softened the company/participant close and swapped the CTA question to match the new resume theme. Preserved voice, emojis (🔹, •), line breaks, and the @[Innovation Challenge®](urn:li:organization:11786165) mention syntax exactly. The attached video asset was not changed. Alternative if Anil prefers less rewrite: keep the original opening two lines and only add the 'more than a resume' stanza.
proposals.suggestedReply: Thanks, Anil — you were right that it leaned too salesy. I reworked it around your point: it’s less about applying for a job and more about applying your skills to prove you’re a fit, showing the human capability and purpose a resume can’t. I also worked in the idea that the best programs signal to everyone who takes part — even those who don’t get a callback — that they’re more than a resume. Have a look and let me know if it lands right.
